top_authentic_signals.name: Spectral Artifacts
top_authentic_signals.summary: The Six-Lens model scored this image 76.2% authentic and 23.8% AI, a extremely high-confidence finding toward real camera capture.
top_authentic_signals.what_found: Across all six lenses, the model returned only 23.8% AI probability, consistent with real camera optics. The SRM residuals match expected sensor noise, the FFT spectrum shows natural frequency falloff (no periodic grid artifacts), and the SPAI reconstruction probe behaved the way natural scenes respond, not the way AI-synthesized regions do.
top_authentic_signals.why_it_matters: A 76.2% authenticity score means the image's deepest mathematical structure is consistent with physical lens optics and silicon sensor physics. AI generators produce fundamentally different frequency-domain statistics than cameras, and those differences persist even when the image looks visually convincing.
top_authentic_signals.caveat: Heavy JPEG compression, aggressive resizing, or strong image filters can partially destroy the frequency-domain signals this model depends on, potentially softening a confident AI detection into an inconclusive result. Conversely, very new or unusual AI generators not present in training data may produce lower-than-expected scores.

top_ai_signals.name: Metadata & Provenance
top_ai_signals.summary: The file's embedded provenance marks it as AI-generated.
top_ai_signals.what_found: The provenance metadata flags this as trained-algorithmic (AI-generated) media.
top_ai_signals.why_it_matters: Provenance markers like C2PA are an industry-standard, hard-to-fake trace written by the generator itself. Finding one is among the strongest provenance signals available.
top_ai_signals.caveat: Provenance can be stripped or, rarely, forged. Absence of a marker is not proof of authenticity.

top_inconclusive_signals.name: Lighting Physics & Contrast Geometry
top_inconclusive_signals.summary: The lighting is balanced and well-behaved (254/255 range, 25.7/255 mean, 0.007% clipping) - matching both a well-exposed real photo and a capable AI generator.
top_inconclusive_signals.what_found: The image has a 254/255 dynamic range, 25.7/255 mean brightness, and only 0.007% clipped highlights with 0.126% crushed shadows. This balanced exposure is realistic-looking but not diagnostic - it fits equally well for a careful real photograph and a modern AI generator.
top_inconclusive_signals.why_it_matters: Lighting is most useful when it's either suspiciously perfect (AI) or clearly clipping (real). A balanced middle-ground doesn't give us enough to work with, so this signal defers to others.
top_inconclusive_signals.caveat: HDR post-processing, tone mapping, strong flash, and professional retouching can all alter exposure profiles - introducing 'AI-like' qualities into real photos or vice versa.

top_inconclusive_signals.name: Thermal Noise & Sensor Consistency
top_inconclusive_signals.summary: The noise profile is ambiguous - variance 912.6, 11.0% smooth blocks - midrange values that could belong to either a compressed real photo or a noise-augmented AI image.
top_inconclusive_signals.what_found: The image has variance 912.6 and 11.0% flat blocks - neither extreme enough to trigger a clear verdict. This ambiguity typically means the image has been compressed, resized, or otherwise processed in a way that erased the original noise fingerprint.
top_inconclusive_signals.why_it_matters: When noise falls in the middle range, it can belong to either side - meaning this signal cannot meaningfully contribute to the verdict. The other detectors carry more weight here.
top_inconclusive_signals.caveat: Heavy compression, denoising, upscaling, or added grain filters can all change the noise profile independently of whether the image was generated or photographed.

top_inconclusive_signals.summary: ELA found essentially no compression residual (mean: 0.28, max: 13.00). The image's original quality setting is too close to the test quality for ELA to produce meaningful results.
top_inconclusive_signals.what_found: Re-saving this image at quality 90 produced a mean residual of only 0.28 - effectively nothing. The amplification scale needed to visualize the heatmap is 19.6x, confirming the actual ELA energy is negligible. ELA is blind to images saved at the same quality as the test - no evidence can be extracted here.
top_inconclusive_signals.why_it_matters: A zero residual means ELA has nothing to report - not that the image is clean, just that this particular test found nothing actionable. Other detectors carry the forensic weight here.
top_inconclusive_signals.caveat: ELA detects editing and compression inconsistency, not AI generation. Social media uploads, repeated saves, and WhatsApp forwarding all degrade this test. It's treated as a weak supporting check.
